To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrocatalysis of H2O(2) by horseradish peroixdase (HRP)-modified electrode is affected by the different interactions between HRP and the different configurations of the nanocomposites.
the LAM-CS@HPR/dpAu/GC biosensor has the best performance among these three kinds of biosensors.
the biosensor based on L-arginine and MWCNT nanocomposites has better electrocatalytical activity to H2PO2 compared with the biosensor based d-arginine or MWCNT nancomposites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the enantioselectivity of the interaction between HRP and chiral amino acid.
the application of chiral amino acid and multi-walled CNTs as matrices to monitor H2O2.
the application of chiral amino acids to monitor hydrogen peroxidase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrocatalysis of H2O(2) on the biosensor was dependent on the configuration of the nanocomposites, and the biosensor based on LAM-CS@ HRP/dpAu/ GCE had better electrocatalysis to H(2)O(2).
l-arginine functionalization on MWCNTs has a significant effect on the electrochemical behavior of the biosensor and it is a promising method for the development of biosensor.
LAM-CS@HP/dpAu/GC electrode has a better electrocatalysis to H2O than the other two electrodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LAM-CS@H2O2 biosensors based on chiral arginine enantiomer functionalized multi-walls carbon nanotubes are more suitable to monitor the hydrogen peroxide in the range of low concentrations.

the chiral arginine can be used as the chiral matrix to immobilize the HRP on the surface of electrode, the biosensor based on L-arginine-MWCNTs-HRP showed better catalytic activity for the H2O2 detection than the other two biosensors.

the biosensors based on l-Arg-MCNTs and d-Arg-MWCNt have the same sensitivity to H2O, but the biosensors based d-Arg-MCNT have a higher detection limit than the biosensor based on L-Arg-MCNT, which may be due to the different interactions between H2O2 and HRP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enantioselectivity of HRP can be utilized to design and construct a novel chiral H2O2 sensor.
chiral arginine functionalized MWCNTs can be used as a novel matrix to immobilize enzyme for H2O2 detection.
the biosensor based on LAM-CS@H2O2 has a good electrocatalytic performance for the detection of H2O 2 and has a good prospect in practical applications.
